card.name: The word causal before relationship
card.fires_on: The word "causal" right after "a", "the" or "possible" in safety statements about whether an event was caused by a drug. It also fires weakly on "patient" in a similar "may be related to" statement.

modes.label: causal relationship
modes.description: "causal" introduces a statement that a link to the drug is unproven or unknown.
modes.example: A<< causal>> relationship has not been established.

modes.label: causal role or link
modes.description: "causal" is followed by role or link when raising a possible drug cause for symptoms.
modes.example: consideration should be given to a possible<< causal>> role of the stimulant, and discontin

modes.label: patient before may be related
modes.description: "patient" appears in a clause asking whether symptoms may be related to the illness.
modes.example: the emergence of these symptoms in any given<< patient>> may be related to the illness being treated

card.writes: It pushes the next word toward "related" or "relate" forms and away from "connected" forms.
card.plain: It spots the word "causal" in phrases saying a drug's role in an event is uncertain.
